mapping.rule: each offered tool is the function object {name, description or "", parameters or {}}, a null field read as absent, every other field (strict, defer_loading, any other key) dropped; the encoder renders that object. A strict tool's parameters are the recipe's normalized schema: each type keeps only its own keywords, in the recipe's key order, every object lists all of its properties as required and sets additionalProperties to false, and a missing schema is the empty object {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "additionalProperties": false, "required": []}; an unknown, duplicate or partial required list, additionalProperties true, an object without properties below the top level, a node of no known shape and a top level other than an object are refused with the recipe's messages. Strict and non-strict tools together, and any response_format beside strict tools, are refused among the tools the declared tools.choice policy leaves, as the recipe checks after its named-choice filtering

mapping.rule: no generation header follows a final assistant turn, which ends with the end-of-sentence token, so such a request is refused (final-assistant-turn) unless the turn is continued, which renders it without that token: by prefix: true on it, as the recipe asks for a continuation, or by continue_final_message. The transport reads prefix for every model, as continue_final_message, and refuses it on any other message with the recipe's text. In thinking mode a continued turn with no content and no calls leaves its reasoning open, <think>{reasoning} without </think>, as the recipe renders a prefix turn, so the completion continues the reasoning; the encoder closes it, so the corpus reference removes that </think> from the encoder's text. The recipe refuses prefix beside tools or json_object, but the format cannot tell prefix from continue_final_message, so a continuation stays served there. The recipe appends a header after every request but a prefix continuation. System messages alone render as the encoder renders them: a later system message is followed by the header, so two or more are served and match the encoder, and the recipe serves them too; only a lone system message, after R5 drops empty ones, has no header and is refused
